sentences.text: Maxakalisaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur distinguished by a long neck and tail, as well as ridged teeth, a feature unusual among sauropods. It also possessed osteoderms, a trait shared by many other titanosaurs.

The type specimen represents an animal approximately 12.1 meters long and weighing an estimated 5 tons, though a juvenile specimen was estimated at 13 meters long and 9 tons, suggesting adults may have reached 20 meters.
Alexander Kellner stated that Maxakalisaurus is the largest dinosaur ever described in Brazil.
Its unusually grooved teeth stand out as a rare adaptation within the sauropod lineage.

The genus Maxakalisaurus was discovered in 1998 in the Adamantina Formation of Minas Gerais, Brazil, and Alexander W. A. Kellner and his team formally described Maxakalisaurus topai as a new genus and species in 2006.

Excavations for the holotype skeleton took place between 1998 and 2002 along a road 45 km west of Prata, Minas Gerais, where fossils recovered from the type locality include remains belonging to both an adult and a subadult individual. The holotype specimen, cataloged as MN 5013-V, was housed at the National Museum of Brazil.

Many elements of the holotype were destroyed in the National Museum of Brazil fire on September 2, 2018, though some survived, after the specimen was stored at the National Museum of Brazil in Rio de Janeiro before being destroyed in the 2018 fire.
A new specimen containing a dentary and teeth was described as belonging to Maxakalisaurus in 2016.
South American sauropods, including Maxakalisaurus, evolved greater diversity and unusual traits due to a lack of significant competition.
Maxakalisaurus is the genus name for this extinct animal, and the specific species name is topai, making the full name Maxakalisaurus topai.

Maxakalisaurus is classified within the family Saltasauridae and belongs to the tribe Aeolosaurini. Phylogenetic analysis places Maxakalisaurus within Aeolosaurini alongside Aeolosaurus and Gondwanatitan.

Maxakalisaurus lived in the Adamantina Formation of Brazil during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, in what is now South America. The fossil belongs to the Baru Formation of the Late Cretaceous, dating to approximately 80 million years ago, and Maxakalisaurus lived approximately 80 million years ago.
The time range for Maxakalisaurus is estimated from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
Researchers have found bones that appear to belong to larger dinosaurs in Brazil, but these have not yet been assembled for scientific description.
